_note: Frozen content for design review. Statement-led family — one sentence per page set at display size in a condensed face, with the clause it turns on carrying the mint.
brief: A guide to protecting your attention

slots.eyebrow: A guide to getting one thing finished
slots.tagline: It is what you have already refused. Six pages on removing the things that were going to interrupt you anyway.
slots.item1: Why your best hours are the ones you give away
slots.item2: What an open tab actually costs
slots.item3: The refusal that makes the rest unnecessary
slots.coverNote: None of this requires an app

slots.bodyLine1: Focus is choosing one thing and letting
slots.bodyLine3: It is not a state you enter by trying harder. It is the consequence of having decided, in advance, what you are not going to do today.
slots.f1Body: Nobody concentrates their way out of an unclear priority.
slots.f2Body: Everything else still gets done, later, and knowing that is what allows the first thing to finish.

slots.bodyLine3: Every notification you can receive is a decision you have to make, and you make it whether or not you open the message.
slots.f1Body: Turning it off costs nothing. Resisting it costs something every time.
slots.f2Body: A phone in another room is a different phone from the same one face down.

slots.bodyLine1: Your best two hours are usually
slots.bodyLine3: Most people give their sharpest part of the day to email and meetings, then attempt the difficult work on whatever is left of it.
slots.f1Body: Book it before anyone else can, and treat it as immovable.
slots.f2Body: Correspondence at four in the afternoon is indistinguishable from correspondence at nine.

slots.bodyLine1: The hard part is never the work, it is
slots.bodyLine3: Beginning is the expensive step, which is why the tidying, the reading and the tooling all feel so urgent right before it.
slots.f1Body: A rough first version removes the blank page, which was the actual obstacle.
slots.f2Body: Stopping mid-sentence gives tomorrow a running start instead of a cold one.

slots.bodyLine3: Asking takes a minute and answering takes twenty, because the person answering has to rebuild the context they had just finished assembling.
slots.f1Body: Twice a day is responsive. Continuously is a second job.
slots.f2Body: The most helpful person on a team is often the one who finished something.

slots.bodyLine1: None of this works if you have not
slots.bodyLine3: Every technique here protects a priority. Applied without one, they produce a very well-defended day in which nothing important happens.
slots.f1Body: The hour is only worth defending once you know what it is for.
slots.f2Body: If you cannot name it in a sentence, the problem is not your concentration.

slots.tagline: One sentence on what matters today, and two hours in the calendar with nothing else in them.
slots.closingLine: The technique is trivial. Deciding what deserves the hours is the whole difficulty.
slots.signoff: No app required, which is why it works
